name: Parapet Gate

stars.name: Parapet
stars.notes: Young, blazing white star pouring ultraviolet and flare activity across the inner system; no world within five orbits is survivable unshielded.

planets.name: Torchline
planets.notes: Daylit lava seas under a shredded atmosphere; probe surveys last minutes before the Flare Choir cooks their electronics.

planets.name: Slagwork
planets.notes: Strip-mined bare by robotic trains during the first rush; now exhausted and officially written off.

planets.name: Glasshouse
planets.notes: Its surface fused to natural glass sheets by ancient flares; optics-grade panes are cut robotically and shipped out by the kiloton.

planets.name: Kilnrange
planets.notes: Tectonically furious shield world; the fleet quarantines it after a survey team's unexplained loss.

planets.name: Firstwall
planets.notes: Runaway-greenhouse rock with domed research shells maintained by rotating crews; no permanent settlement is possible or wanted.

planets.name: Rampart
planets.notes: The heart of the system: hydrogen skimming, fuel cracking, and the Grand Anchorage moored among its cloud-piercing moons.

planets.name: Secondwall
planets.notes: Patrol giant whose moonlets host the picket squadrons screening the anchorage's blind side.

planets.name: Icepick
planets.notes: Water mine for the entire fleet; its harvest convoys run to Rampart on a four-day cycle.

planets.name: Lastlight
planets.notes: Outermost rock carrying the stealth early-warning array pointed at everything the Hegemony does not control.

anomalies.name: The Flare Choir
anomalies.notes: Resonant magnetic oscillations amplify every stellar flare into an electronics-killing wavefront; it is why the inner system is empty and why the fleet parks safely behind orbit 5.

asteroid_belts.name: Cutlass Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Armor-grade iron under exclusive Hegemony Navy lease; civilian miners hold legacy contracts nobody dares revoke.

asteroid_belts.name: Vigil Belt
asteroid_belts.notes: Deliberately sown with sensor mines and relay seeds; the fleet calls the belt 'the tripwire.'

stations.name: Grand Anchorage Parapet
stations.notes: Largest naval facility in the Marches: a full ring dock where battle groups form, stage, and depart for the frontier.

stations.name: Skim Depot Seven
stations.notes: Fuel terminal handling tanker traffic; its queues are the system's only civilian spectacle.

stations.name: Picket Station Gamma
stations.notes: Cold-running watch post on the frontier vector; crews volunteer for the quiet and come back talking less.

faction_control.notes: Closed fleet system under total Hegemony control; access requires naval sponsorship, and smuggling attempts average one per month, none successful.

history: Charted young and bright, the system was dismissed as worthless real estate for a century — until the Flare Choir was identified and the inner system revealed as a natural kill-zone.
The Grand Fleet built its anchorage deliberately behind that wall, where no attacking fleet can linger to besiege it.
Every Hegemony offensive in the last thirty years staged out of Rampart's orbit; the ring's construction cranes have never gone dark.
description: A white star too fierce for life burns at the center of nine hard worlds, and the Flare Choir turns the whole inner system into a thunderclap waiting to happen. Beyond that wall, the system opens up: twin gas giants, a working ice mine, and the vast ring of the Grand Anchorage gleaming in Rampart's shadow.

Parapet Gate is the sword-arm of the Hegemony Marches. Battle groups assemble at the ring, tankers stack up at Skim Depot Seven, and the Vigil Belt watches the frontier with a million electronic eyes. Traffic is heavy, disciplined, and overwhelmingly naval — civilian hulls keep to the fuel lanes or get boarded.

The fleet considers the system impregnable, which is exactly what unsettles its own officers: Picket Station Gamma reports approach vectors that resolve to nothing, Kilnrange remains quarantined for reasons redacted even internally, and the Flare Choir has recently begun singing slightly off-key. Nobody at the Anchorage says that part aloud.
